clue.text: Have influence on current parliamentarian decree

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
MP, Member of Parliament
an act is a law passed, a decree

explanation.surface: A sitting member pushes through a decree on the national electricity supply to make their mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To impact something is to affect it, to have a marked effect upon it.

clue.text: One caught in local, not at work

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letter for caught is placed inside the word for a local

parts.note: a local is someone born in the place, a native
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the pub during working hours is clearly not at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' reads as a pub, a common British name for one's neighbourhood bar, but here it is a resident born there.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not at work is idle, doing nothing, hence inactive.

clue.text: Very little paid for source of oil

definitions.meaning: second meaning: groundnuts, which are pressed for cooking oil

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests poorly paid oil workers; the two halves are separate senses of one plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is slang for a trivial sum of money, and the nuts themselves yield groundnut oil.

clue.text: Card one of the people dramatically played

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an eccentric or amusing person, 'a real card'

definitions.text: one of the people dramatically played
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a role in a play, a person portrayed on stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' and 'played' together suggest a card game; card is in fact an old word for a comic oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is both a colourful eccentric person and a part an actor takes in a drama.

clue.text: Successive notes I had put outside and set apart

indicators.note: the contraction is placed around the run of notes, so it sits on the outside

parts.note: I'D is the contraction of I had
sol, la and te follow one another in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician recalls playing a run of notes and then being shut away on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate from others, so isolated means kept apart.

clue.text: Location in West End anyone can use for their address

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a well-known spot in central London, at the corner of Hyde Park

definitions.text: anyone can use for their address
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a place where any member of the public may make a speech, address meaning a talk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a postal address shared by all; it means a public speech. The spot is in the north-east corner of Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous patch of Hyde Park is a traditional venue for free open-air oratory and debate.

clue.text: Branch office's head in a state of uncertainty

parts.note: a limb is a large branch of a tree

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter, so only the opening of office is used

parts.note: the word office, whose first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A regional branch is left in suspense after its manager becomes unsure of the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is an intermediate state of unresolved waiting or neglect.

clue.text: Matched, having the same score for each team included

indicators.note: the word for each side is placed within the word for level

parts.note: teams level on points are tied
in scores such as 'two all', all means for each side

explanation.surface: A sports report of a drawn match where both sides finish on equal points.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that tally agree with each other, so tallied means corresponded.

clue.text: Be condescending about son's intention

indicators.note: the word for stooping goes around the letter for son

parts.note: to deign is to stoop to do something beneath one
S for son

explanation.surface: A parent looks down on their son's plans with a patronising air.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a plan or purpose, as in 'by design', meaning on purpose.

clue.text: Positions before battle — start of drama in progress before Waterloo etc

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: Act I is the first act of a play
something happening now is on
Waterloo is one of London's main railway stations, given as an example

explanation.surface: A war film opens with troops taking position just before the Battle of Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests Wellington's battle, which fits 'battle' nicely, but it is the London terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Action stations is the military order for crew to take their combat posts.

clue.text: Sudden fall of snow disturbing a mostly calm haven

indicators.note: a calm scene that is disturbed is thrown into disorder, signalling these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the word calm, cut short before the shuffle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peaceful mountain refuge is shattered by a sudden snowslide.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow sliding rapidly down a mountainside.

clue.text: Announced posts for about 50% of the population

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word for posts is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: post is letters, also called mail

explanation.surface: A public notice about jobs available for half the community.
explanation.definitionFit: Men make up roughly half of humanity, so this is a playful statistical description.

clue.text: Wave from a friend in Paris on back street

indicators.note: the French phrase comes after, sitting on the reversed letters
the street abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: ST, as in addresses
un ami is French for a friend

explanation.surface: A friend in Paris waves from the back street as you pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' looks like a greeting gesture but is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake or landslide.

clue.text: Intelligent ruler wrapping present

indicators.note: the monarch is wrapped around the word for the current time

parts.note: a king is a monarch
the present moment is now

explanation.surface: A shrewd monarch gift-wraps a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift being wrapped; it is the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing means shrewd and well informed, showing clever awareness.

clue.text: It is switched after very short call

indicators.note: the swapped words come after the single letter

parts.note: V is the short form of very

indicators.note: the two words are swapped round into a different order

parts.note: the two words taken as written, then put the other way round

explanation.surface: A telephone line is switched over after a very brief call.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to pay them a visit, so a call is a short social visit.

clue.text: Two men, and not a woman, in part of France

parts.note: Norm is a man's name, the first of the two
Andy is the second man; Andy could be short for a woman's name like Andrea, so the clue rules that out

explanation.surface: A couple of men, rather than a woman, are holidaying in a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: The two names run together; 'not a woman' warns against reading the first as Norma.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a region of northern France on the English Channel coast.

clue.text: In charge in club, liable to prove poisonous

indicators.note: the letters for in charge go inside the club's name

parts.note: Arsenal is a London football club
IC, in charge

explanation.surface: The man in charge at a football club proves to be a toxic presence.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenical means containing arsenic, the classic poison of crime fiction.

clue.text: Racket set up inside secret society in tropical island

indicators.note: the reversed noise is placed within the society

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese criminal secret society

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a din is a loud noise, a racket

explanation.surface: A criminal gang runs a protection racket on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' reads as a criminal scheme, which fits the secret society, but it means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago in the southern Caribbean.

clue.text: Pace trio varied — some of Mozart's music is like that

definitions.text: some of Mozart's music is like that

indicators.note: altered or changed about, so the letters of the two words are reordered

parts.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written, are the material

explanation.surface: A trio plays Mozart at a varied pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart wrote many operas, so much of his music is in the style of opera.

clue.text: Walk carefully on weed in field

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: to pad is to walk softly
dock is a broad-leaved weed

explanation.surface: Tiptoeing over weeds while crossing a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field, often for horses.

clue.text: Police officer having a meal half-heartedly

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its doubled middle letter; half of it is dropped

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A policeman eats his dinner without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Super is short for superintendent, a senior British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A super is a police superintendent, a senior officer rank.

clue.text: Part of speech from prof, no dunce, without notes

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the note letters are struck out of the phrase

parts.note: the three words run together, already without F and D, two of the musical notes the clue strikes out
C and E are musical notes, the last two of the four removed

explanation.surface: A professor, no fool, lectures on grammar without any notes.
explanation.walkthrough: All four notes go: strike F, D, C and E from the run of letters in 'prof no dunce' and what is left, in order, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronoun is a word class standing in for a noun, such as he or it.

clue.text: Endlessly seek advice from diplomat

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to consult someone is to ask their advice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps asking a diplomat for guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is an official representing a country's interests in a foreign city.

clue.text: In part, holds altitude, as experienced crewman

indicators.note: only a part of the phrase is used, the answer sitting within its letters

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of holds and the start of altitude

explanation.surface: A seasoned sailor holds the ship at altitude, or perhaps a pilot holds height.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran sailor, a seaman of long experience.

clue.text: Old weapon found in a river bank

parts.note: taken as written
a bank of seats or keys is a row of them

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds an ancient weapon on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrow, shot from a bow, is an ancient missile weapon.

clue.text: Managed to continue providing capital earlier for some Asians

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to go on is to carry on

explanation.surface: A manager keeps funding something for Asian investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is a capital city. Rangoon (now Yangon) was the capital of Burma until 2005.

clue.text: Immerse foreign coin in acid to clean thoroughly

indicators.note: to immerse something is to dip it into liquid, so one piece goes inside the other
names the word that the coin is dipped into

parts.note: sour means acidic in taste
C for cent, a foreign coin to a British setter

explanation.surface: A cleaning tip: soak a tarnished coin in acid to clean it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub hard with something abrasive.

clue.text: Put too many into lift, say — more than three?

definitions.text: Put too many into lift, say

parts.note: over means more than
from the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'

explanation.surface: A lift sign warns against cramming in more than three people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the proverb: if three's a crowd, more than three is over a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcrowd is to pack too many people into a space such as an elevator.

clue.text: In the same way, enjoy having knowledge

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
wise means learned

explanation.surface: Someone who loves learning feels the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise is an adverb meaning similarly, also.

clue.text: Repeatedly copied single in newer kind of record

indicators.note: the word for single goes inside the disc's abbreviation

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, superseded vinyl records
lone means single, solitary

explanation.surface: A hit single is copied over and over onto a CD.
